content.text:
The main gap is that the log shows the storage plumbing but almost nothing about what the agent is doing. Of the ~20 lines in your example, about 13 are git ref bookkeeping from `src/storage/sync.ts` and `src/worktree.ts`. Each "pushed abc1234" stands for something the agent did, like a tool call, a reply, or a steer, but the log only prints the commit hash. I'd make three changes:

1. Show what the agent does.
2. Move the plumbing out of the default log, or fold it away.
3. Rewrite the remaining lines so they read as plain sentences.

## 1. Show what the agent does

Print one line per event in the agent loop, cut to about 120 characters:

```
▶ Turn 1 — @cv: "let's make the selected changes in this PR"
  claude-opus-5.5 · thinking: medium
  🔧 bash        git diff main...HEAD --stat                       ✓ 1.2s
  🔧 read        src/worktree.ts (1–200)                            ✓
  🔧 edit        src/worktree.ts (2 changes)                        ✓
  🔧 bash        npm test                                           ✗ exit 1 · 38s
  🔧 bash        npm test                                           ✓ 41s
  💬 "I've applied the changes from the review; tests pass…"
  ✓ Turn 1 done — 14 tool calls, 3m12s, 182k in / 9k out tokens ($0.41)
```

- **Where to hook in:** the harness already writes every tool call and result as an entry. `Thread.ranTools()` reads them back with `root.entries()`. We can follow the same entries as they are committed, or subscribe to the harness's events if it has them, and print a short line for each one.
- **What each line shows:** the tool name plus its key argument (the command for `bash`, the path for `read`/`edit`/`write`, the first line for `typescript`), then ✓/✗ and how long it took. Tool output is never printed. It can be huge and may contain secrets.
- **Assistant text:** only the first line, quoted. The full reply already goes into the comment.
- **Steers and questions:** comments that arrive mid-run, and questions waiting for an answer, get their own lines, e.g. `↪ new comment from @x joined the run` and `❓ asked: …`.

## 2. Move the plumbing out of the default log

| Line today | Proposal |
|---|---|
| `refs/pi/threads/45: pushed 7787a77` (× N) | Debug only (`core.debug`, shown when "Enable debug logging" is on). Replace with one line at the end: `Saved thread: 9 pushes, now at 7701574`. Warn only if a push fails or is retried. |
| `Saved the working tree as 5f5a17d on refs/pi/worktrees/45` | Debug, plus a final `Working tree saved (3 files changed) as 8b3392f`. Keep the "skipped N untracked files" warning visible. |
| `pushed 28f9549 with refs/pi/worktrees/45 at 21fde8e` | Debug. |
| Extension install/load lines, agent dir, `GH_TOKEN`, trust | Put them in a collapsed `::group::Setup` block with a one-line summary outside it, e.g. `Setup: pit v0.35.1 (typescript tool), project not trusted, 4.1s`. |
| `pit has a pi-durable extension … loading only the pi-durable one…` | Shorter wording, inside the setup group. |

## 3. Plain wording and structure

- `Thread refs/pi/threads/45: since 2026-11-12T07:01:35.000Z` becomes `Continuing the conversation on #45 (started 12 Nov, 3 earlier runs)`. A new thread gets `Starting a new conversation on #45`.
- `refs/pi/worktrees/45: new on origin` becomes nothing, or `No saved working tree yet` in debug.
- `Running pi agent for: <task>` becomes the turn header in section 1, so it includes who asked and links to the comment.
- Fold each turn into its own `::group::` so a long run stays readable. The single-line turn summary stays outside the group, so the collapsed view reads like a timeline.
- Failures (`pi execution failed`, timeouts, rejected pushes) stay `::error::` / `::warning::` annotations, so they show up in the run summary page.

## 4. Job summary

`deps.summary` is used today only for notifications and the "how to read the thread" block. It could also get a small table per run: turns, tool calls by tool, failed tool calls, tokens/cost, duration, the files changed in the working-tree snapshot, and a link to the posted comment. That makes the summary page a quick overview, with the step log there for detail.

## 5. A `log-level` input

Add `log-level: quiet | normal | verbose`:
- **`quiet`:** turn headers and summaries, warnings, errors.
- **`normal`** (default): everything above.
- **`verbose`:** tool-call arguments in full, plus all ref pushes and snapshots. Turning on GitHub's debug logging would also enable this level.

## Suggested order

1. Tool-call and turn lines (section 1). Most of the value is here.
2. Move ref push and snapshot lines to debug, with a final summary line (section 2). It's a small change in `sync.ts` and `worktree.ts`.
3. Setup group and per-turn groups.
4. Job summary table, then the `log-level` input.

I haven't changed any code or committed anything, since this issue is asking for options. If you tell me which of these you want, I can open a PR.
